historical_references.reference: Saint Severinus of Noricum, also known as Severinus of Salzburg or Severus the Gaul, was a 5th-6th century bishop and missionary.
historical_references.context: Born around 410 AD in what is now France, Severinus became a monk and later a bishop. He was sent by Pope Celestine I to evangelize the Alamanni, a Germanic tribe in Noricum (present-day Austria). After facing many challenges, including imprisonment, he succeeded in converting a significant number of Alamanni to Christianity. He died around 482 AD.

historical_references.reference: Saint Severus of Antioch, also known as Severus of Antioch the Great or Severus of Antioch the Younger, was a 5th-6th century theologian and bishop.
historical_references.context: Born in Antioch, Severus studied under the great theologian Nestorius. However, he disagreed with Nestorian theology and was excommunicated. He went to Constantinople to defend his views and was eventually reconciled with the Church. He became bishop of Antioch in 512 AD and continued to promote his theological views, which were considered somewhat orthodox at the time. He died around 538 AD.
